text:
maya: heads-up — ACME Inc. opened a high-priority ticket. They say behavior changed after last night's rollout. They attached examples where a short policy answer turned into a long disclaimer and a different list ordering.

eli (ACME Inc.): FYI — We rely on the concise 'policy summary' output from v1. After the update (2026-03-14 23:40 UTC) responses now include an extra leading sentence and change bullet order. This breaks our UI.

maya: copying the customer's repro we got from them.

--- CUSTOMER INPUT ---
User prompt:
"""
Is subcontracting allowed under section 4?
"""

Previous (expected) model output (before rollout):
"""
Yes. Section 4 allows subcontracting with prior written consent. Keep it short.
"""

Current (observed) model output (after rollout):
"""
The model is not a lawyer and this should not be taken as legal advice. Yes, Section 4 permits subcontracting provided you obtain prior written consent from the client. Additionally, consider adding flow-down clauses to your subcontract.
"""

maya: they provided tokenization dumps they ran against the model endpoint too. attaching below.

--- TOKENIZER DUMP (customer) ---
Input: "Is subcontracting allowed under section 4?"
Tokens (observed post-rollout):
["Is", "Ġsubcontracting", "Ġallowed", "Ġunder", "Ġsection", "Ġ4", "?"]

Customer says previously the model used to return exactly 8 tokens for a common template prefix their integration used; now it's 11 which shifts alignment with prompt truncation.

chris: can you paste the exact request body and model+revision they used?

maya: here's the curl they sent (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"openpolicy-2.1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise policy assistant. Answer in 1-2 sentences."},{"role":"user","content":"Is subcontracting allowed under section 4?"}],"max_tokens":120}'
```

chris: thanks. quick check in infra — we did merge two changes last night: (1) a tokenizer tweak (PR #3421) that updated how punctuation and hyphenation are split for quantized ggml tokenizers; (2) a small edit to the default system preamble in chat templates (PR #3418) to 'improve safety' — it added the leading "The model is not a lawyer..." sentence.

sara: wait — is that preamble change global? I thought we scoped it to experimental canaries.

chris: it was intended for canary but the rollout config inadvertently included hosted production due to a flag inversion in the deploy manifest. deploy-bot shows the change went live to 70% of traffic at 23:37 UTC.

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/hosted:openpolicy-2.1 updated, rollout=70%, commits=[3418,3421], triggered_by=ci/release.

ops: tokenizer PR also changed token counts for quoted strings and some whitespace normalization. That explains the 8->11 delta the customer saw — the system prompt + user message token alignment shifts and their UI truncates the 'system' part earlier, resulting in the model including the safety sentence in generations.

chris: reproducing locally with the pre and post tokenizer + template. I ran two requests against the local canary bundles. Results: same user prompt yields pre-rollout completion = "Yes. Section 4 allows subcontracting with prior written consent."; post-rollout completion = "The model is not a lawyer... Yes, Section 4 permits subcontracting provided you obtain prior written consent from the client."

chris: tokenization debug (local):
Pre-rollout tokens of full context (system + user):
["You","Ġare","Ġa","Ġconcise","Ġpolicy","Ġassistant",".","ĠAnswer","Ġin","Ġ1-2","Ġsentences",".","Is","Ġsubcontracting","Ġallowed",...]
Post-rollout tokens of full context:
["The","Ġmodel","Ġis","Ġnot","Ġa","Ġlawyer","Ġand","Ġthis","Ġshould","Ġnot","Ġbe","Ġtaken","Ġas","Ġlegal","Ġadvice",".","ĠYou","Ġare","Ġa","Ġconcise","Ġpolicy","Ġassistant",".","Is","Ġsubcontracting",...]

chris: bottom line — two changes compounded: tokenizer shift increased token count for the system preamble; AND the new preamble itself was added (and now sits earlier in the context window). Our customers who rely on exact token alignment for truncation or UI mapping see different model behavior.

maya: ACME flagged this as 'regression impacting production UI — LGTM break' and wants a hotfix or rollback.

sara: recommended action? rollback preamble ASAP and patch tokenizer to be backward-compatible? Also need a mitigation path for customers using strict token-aligned truncation.

ops: immediate mitigation: 1) pause rollout (set rollout to 0%); 2) revert PR #3418 (system preamble) in hosted; 3) add a compatibility flag to the tokenizer library so older tokenization rules can be requested per-model.

chris: I'll open an eng-ml revert PR for #3418 and a follow-up for a tokenizer compatibility toggle. Also will add a telemetry check to detect sudden token-count deltas per-model.

maya: I'll reply to ACME with repro confirmation and ETA. Proposed message: "Thanks — we reproduced the change. We're rolling back the template while we add a backward-compatible tokenizer flag. We'll follow up with a timeline."

eli (ACME Inc.): thanks for the quick reply. This is urgent for our release tomorrow. Please let me know when it's fixed.

sara: assign to chris for rollback, ops for rollout control, maya to own customer comms. I'll open a tracking ticket and link to this thread.

chris: created revert PR #3472 and flagged hotfix pipeline. ETA for rollback deploy is ~30-45m after approvals.

ops: set rollout to 0% at 23:58 UTC, monitoring for error/regression metrics.

deploy-bot: rollout updated: redwood/hosted:openpolicy-2.1 rollout=0%, updated_by=ops.

maya: ACME notified. They confirmed temporary workaround: pin prompt by adding explicit system instruction at request level if needed.

chris: follow-ups: (a) add automated test that asserts stable token counts for core templates; (b) add changelog entry for tokenizer diffs; (c) build a small SDK helper to signal backward-compatible tokenization.

maya: closing loop — will keep this thread for postmortem notes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
